title: Postal, telecom and government employees
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The Bharatiya Postal Employees Federation, the Indian Telecom Employees Federation and the Kendriya Karamchari Mahasangh.
body:
BMS has long been active among employees of government departments. Among its federations are the **Bharatiya Postal Employees Federation**, the **Indian Telecom Employees Federation**, the **Kendriya Karamchari Mahasangh** (central government employees) and the **Rashtriya Rajya Karamchari Mahasangh** (State government employees).

## The postal worker

The post office is the oldest public service delivering to every village. Postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks reach places where banks and couriers do not. Unions have raised the status of Gramin Dak Sevaks, whose service conditions differ from those of departmental employees.

## Telecom

After the corporatisation of BSNL and MTNL, the questions have been the revival of the companies, the fate of employees and pensioners and the retention of public sector presence in telecom.

## Government employees

Their major issues have included the **old pension scheme**, the 8th Pay Commission, dearness allowance and regularisation of contract staff. Government employees' federations also took part in the consultations on the Unified Pension Scheme announced in 2024.

## What unites the three

These are people who serve the citizen directly. BMS argues that a government that respects its own employees is better able to serve the people.
